Here in this article, we show how to use the package's function
`discoveryGraph` to plot when the species of any plant family or genus were
discovered, and when their synonyms were published. The graphic has two
panels: the number of species described and the number of synonyms published
in each decade (or any other period). While `accGraph` shows the cumulative
discovery of species, `discoveryGraph` shows when the taxonomic work, i.e.
describing new species and renaming them, was most intense.\

A species is counted in the year of its basionym, i.e. its oldest homotypic
name, which is the year the species was discovered. For example, a species
described in 1805 and transferred to another genus in 2001 counts as
discovered in 1805.\

\

# Setup

Install the latest development version of __expowo__ from
[GitHub](https://github.com/):

``` r
#install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("DBOSlab/expowo")
```
```{r package load, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(expowo)
```

\

# 1. Mining the species list with synonyms

`discoveryGraph` needs the accepted species and their synonyms, with the
publication of each name. Use `powoSpecies` with `synonyms = TRUE`. The first
search downloads the data of the World Checklist of Vascular Plants (about
90 MB) only once, so any following search takes a few seconds.\

```{r, eval = FALSE}
fab <- powoSpecies(family = "Fabaceae",
                   synonyms = TRUE,
                   verbose = FALSE)
```

\

# 2. Plotting species discovery per decade

Just provide the output of `powoSpecies` to `discoveryGraph`. The busiest
decade of each panel is labelled. Setting `save = TRUE` writes the graphic
within a subfolder named after the current date, in any of the formats JPG,
PDF, PNG or TIFF.\

```{r, eval = FALSE}
discoveryGraph(inputdf = fab,
               save = TRUE,
               dir = "results_discoveryGraph",
               filename = "discovery_graph_Fabaceae",
               format = "png")
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, out.width = "620px", fig.cap = "FIGURE 1. Number of Fabaceae species described (top) and synonyms published (bottom) per decade."}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/discovery_graph_Fabaceae.png", dpi = 300)
```

\

Legume species have been described at a steady pace for two centuries, with
peaks in the 1830s-1840s, the time of the works of G. Bentham and of E.
Boissier on the flora of the Orient, and again since the 1980s. Synonyms, in
turn, peak in the 1890s: more than half of the synonyms published in that
decade (3,545 of 6,137) come from Kuntze's _Revisio Generum Plantarum_ (1891).
The last bars are lower because the current decade is not over yet.\

\

# 3. Choosing the length of each period

For smaller families, decades may hold too few names. The argument `bin` sets
the number of years in each bar, e.g. 25 years for Lecythidaceae.\

```{r, eval = FALSE}
lecy <- powoSpecies(family = "Lecythidaceae",
                    synonyms = TRUE,
                    verbose = FALSE)

discoveryGraph(inputdf = lecy,
               bin = 25,
               save = TRUE,
               dir = "results_discoveryGraph",
               filename = "discovery_graph_Lecythidaceae_25years",
               format = "png")
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, out.width = "620px", fig.cap = "FIGURE 2. Number of Lecythidaceae species described (top) and synonyms published (bottom) every 25 years."}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/discovery_graph_Lecythidaceae_25years.png", dpi = 300)
```

\

The busiest period for describing Brazil nut species was 1975-1999, and 39%
of the species were described since 1975, reflecting the monographic work on
the family by S. A. Mori, G. T. Prance and colleagues. Most synonyms, in
contrast, were published in 1850-1874 and 1925-1949.\

\

# 4. Using the graphic object

`discoveryGraph` returns a `ggplot` object, so the graphic can be customised
with any function of __ggplot2__. The data of the graphic has the number of
names (`names`) in each period (`period`) for each panel (`what`).\

```{r, eval = FALSE}
p <- discoveryGraph(fab, verbose = FALSE)

# Number of species discovered in each decade
p$data[p$data$what == levels(p$data$what)[1], c("period", "names")]

# Adding a title
p + ggplot2::ggtitle("Discovery of legume species")
```

\

# 5. Reference

Govaerts, R., E. Nic Lughadha, N. Black, R. Turner, and A. Paton. 2021. The
World Checklist of Vascular Plants, a continuously updated resource for
exploring global plant diversity. Scientific Data 8: 215.
